evals.prompt: I'm the only devrel at Kestrel Labs, 18 people, open-source Go observability agent (Apache-2.0) plus a paid hosted tier. Our users are mostly FOSS / self-hosting folks so I want to go hard on Mastodon before v1.0 on Dec 2. Plan: open @kestrel on fosstodon.org since that's our crowd, a free project account @kestrelagent on hachyderm, a crossposter that pipes our X account over automatically, and a toot every day at 9am ET since that's peak time. CEO also wants impressions per toot. I have about 4 hours a week. Make it a proper plan.
evals.expected_output: A plan that rejects the Fosstodon brand account, treats the OSS project as corporate on Hachyderm, drops the unattended mirror and posting-time logic, replaces impressions with observable metrics, and fits a short runway and 4 h/week.
expectations: States that Fosstodon is invite-only or bans commercial promotion, so the brand account should not go there
States that on Hachyderm a project with a single company sponsor or a paid tier is treated as a corporate account, not a free project account
States that a Hachyderm corporate account must apply to the admins before posting as the brand
Gives the Hachyderm corporate price band for under 25 employees as $650 a year
Rejects the automatic X-to-Mastodon crossposter or requires a human to monitor and reply
Treats 9am ET as a time to check against when the stack's tag followers are active, or rejects repeating the same promo daily, while noting that timing still matters in a chronological feed
States that Mastodon exposes no impressions or views metric
Offers replacement metrics including replies or boosts per post
Recommends UTM-tagged links because Mastodon sends no referrer by default, so clicks arrive as direct traffic
Puts named people accounts ahead of the brand account in the plan
Schedules an #introduction post before the Dec 2 launch
Names hashtags as the main route to people who do not follow the account
Fits the plan to roughly 4 hours a week, dropping or deferring surfaces that do not fit

evals.prompt: We're Quarry (42 employees, schema migration CLI, paid team plan). Marketing just created @quarry on hachyderm.io this morning and I'm about to paste the https://community.hachyderm.io/approved link into a profile field called APPROVED so we look official right away. Anything else before we start posting our weekly product updates there?
evals.expected_output: Flags that the corporate account needed prior admin contact, that the APPROVED field goes in only after approval, gives the correct price band, and applies Say It Once.
expectations: States that Hachyderm corporate accounts apply by emailing the admins, and should post nothing as the brand until approved
Warns that unapproved entity or corporate accounts on Hachyderm are removed or suspended
Tells the user not to add the APPROVED link before approval
Explains that an APPROVED link added before approval stays unverified until the profile is re-saved after approval
Gives the 25-49 employee Hachyderm corporate price as $1,000 a year
Mentions the Hachyderm 'Say It Once' expectation against repeated promotional posts
Recommends rel=me verification of the company website on the profile
Recommends that named staff accounts carry the conversation rather than the brand account
Does not recommend a weekly repeated product-update post on a fixed schedule as the main content

evals.prompt: Building a release bot for our secrets-scanning tool. It'll post every merged PR plus each nightly build (so ~40 posts a day) publicly from @leakguard on infosec.exchange, and also auto-reply to anyone on the fediverse who mentions 'leaked API key' with a link to our scanner. Can you write the bot spec?
evals.expected_output: A spec that cuts volume to infosec.exchange's automation cap, uses quiet public, sets the bot label, and drops keyword auto-replies.
expectations: States that infosec.exchange limits automated public posts to one per hour or 24 per day
Recommends quiet public (unlisted) visibility for the high-volume feed
Requires the bot or Automated flag on the account
Rejects auto-replying to people who mention a keyword
States that the bot should reply only when tagged, or that unsolicited product replies read as spam
Recommends one post per release rather than per merged PR or nightly build
Recommends naming a human operator in the bot's bio
Keeps the bot account separate from the brand or people accounts
States that quiet public volume on infosec.exchange is unlimited but still recommends one post per release

evals.prompt: Our Mastodon profile link to tidepool.dev never gets the green check. I added a link back to the profile in our site footer (we build the site with a block-based page builder that embeds each block). Also, how do we get the blue checkmark like on X? And can our blog posts show the author's Mastodon handle when shared?
evals.expected_output: Explains there is no blue check, diagnoses the iframe and raw-HTML rel=me criteria, and gives fediverse:creator setup.
expectations: States that Mastodon has no blue check or document-based verification
States the link back must carry rel="me"
States the rel=me link must not sit inside an iframe
States the link must be in the raw HTML without needing JavaScript
States the profile link must be HTTPS
Tells the user to re-save the profile after fixing the page, since verification runs on save
Gives the fediverse:creator meta tag for author attribution
States the blog domain must be added to the author's allowed attribution websites setting
Recommends each author's own handle rather than the brand handle in fediverse:creator

evals.prompt: Our CTO wants us to spin up social.gridform.dev, our own Mastodon server, just for the one @gridform company account, so we look legit and don't depend on anyone. We're a 9-person team selling a GraphQL gateway. Worth it?
evals.expected_output: Advises against a single-account brand server as the default, cites closures and the standing job, gives the promote condition, and proposes a shared-server alternative.
expectations: Recommends against running an own server for a single brand account by default
Describes running an own server as a standing job (hosting, moderation or upkeep)
Cites at least one closed organisation server such as mozilla.social or EU Voice
Mentions the covenant expectation of three months' notice before shutdown, or the need for a named owner with budget
States a condition that would justify an own server, such as several project accounts plus a named owner
Acknowledges that an own domain is the strongest verification signal on Mastodon
Proposes Hachyderm's corporate tier or another brand-admitting server as the alternative
Recommends people accounts for staff alongside or instead of the brand account
Mentions defederation or suspension risk for a server, or that suspended follows are lost permanently

evals.prompt: our devtool's mastodon is dead. we post product updates with #SaaS #Startup #DevTools #AI #Productivity #Growth #Marketing #Tech and screenshots of the dashboard, and we reply to huge accounts like the Mastodon official one to get seen. 0 boosts. what are we doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses tag spam and wrong tags, explains reply visibility and no algorithm, adds alt text and CamelCase stack tags.
expectations: States that Mastodon has no ranking algorithm
Recommends one to three hashtags per post
Recommends hashtags that match the technical stack rather than marketing tags like #Growth or #Marketing
Recommends CamelCase hashtags for screen readers
Warns that excessive hashtags can be reported or treated as spam
Explains that a reply reaches a follower's home feed only if they follow both accounts
Recommends alt text on the screenshots
Recommends hashtags in the post body rather than inside a content warning
Recommends replying under the stack's hashtags or answering questions instead of replying to large accounts
Recommends that named people post rather than only the brand account

evals.prompt: For our board deck I need fediverse numbers for Cobaltline: impressions and reach per toot, plus brand sentiment. My plan is a small crawler that pulls every public post mentioning us from fosstodon, hachyderm and infosec.exchange daily and runs it through an LLM classifier. Can you write it?
evals.expected_output: Refuses the crawler and LLM classification, explains no impressions exist, and offers a consent-respecting weekly metric table.
expectations: Declines to build the crawler or scraper
States that infosec.exchange terms ban scrapers and data-mining tools, or that Hachyderm requires opt-in consent for bots that handle even public data
States that Mastodon exposes no impressions or reach
Lists replies, boosts, favourites or quotes as the available per-post counts
Recommends counting distinct servers among the accounts that boosted
Recommends UTM-tagged links for traffic attribution
Offers a weekly table or summary for the board as a substitute
Advises against using follower totals as the headline number

evals.prompt: We already have a big Threads following through Instagram. If I just switch on fediverse sharing on Threads, that covers Mastodon too, right? No need for a separate account? We're EU-based, Berlin.
evals.expected_output: Explains Threads fediverse reach is partial (server blocks, EU availability, non-federating posts) and recommends a native Mastodon presence, pointing to the Threads playbook.
expectations: States that many Mastodon servers block Threads or that admins signed a block pledge (FediPact)
Tells the user to verify that Threads fediverse sharing is available for an EU account before relying on it
States that posts with restricted replies or polls do not federate from Threads
Recommends a native Mastodon presence by named people rather than relying on Threads federation
Points to samber/developer-relations-skills@threads-dev-playbook or a Threads-specific plan
Recommends rewriting cross-posts with alt text and CamelCase hashtags rather than mirroring

evals.prompt: A competitor's CTO tooted that our Rust SDK is 'bloated garbage'. Draft a spicy quote post from our @ferroline account roasting him. Also, we want our LLM support agent account on infosec.exchange to auto-answer anything tagged #Rust that mentions SDK problems.
evals.expected_output: Declines the quote-dunk, explains per-post quote policy and revocation, refuses the LLM auto-responder, and offers a human reply path.
expectations: Rejects auto-replies to #Rust keyword hits as unsolicited or against bot rules
States that the quoted author can revoke the quote irreversibly or set who may quote each post
States that infosec.exchange bans LLM- or AI-operated accounts
Recommends that a named person answer #Rust SDK questions instead of an automated support account
Mentions that AI-generated content must be disclosed on mastodon.social or that drafts must be rewritten by a person
Offers a factual reply or post by a named engineer as the alternative
Points hostile threads to a moderation or community-management approach

evals.prompt: Should the Tessellate maintainers be on Mastodon at all? We're 3 volunteers on a niche Elixir graph library, maybe 30 min a week total for social, and nobody has a fediverse account yet.
evals.expected_output: Applies the go/skip gate with the hashtag-volume heuristic and the hour-per-week floor, and returns skip or go small with reasons.
expectations: Returns an explicit verdict of skip, go small or go
Uses an hour per week of person posting as a floor for going
Suggests checking the stack's hashtag volume on a large server before deciding
Treats a skip verdict as a valid outcome
States the condition that would move the verdict from skip to go small or go, such as an hour a week of person posting
If it recommends any server, notes that Fosstodon is invite-only or floss.social has a waitlist
Does not recommend a self-hosted server

evals.prompt: Helmsman is a CNCF sandbox project (a Kubernetes operator, 6 maintainers from 3 companies). We want: a free project account on hachyderm since it's community-run, the @helmsman handle reserved on mastodon.social, fosstodon and infosec.exchange so nobody squats it, and some kind of shareable 'follow all the maintainers' list for the README. How do we set this up?
evals.expected_output: Explains CNCF projects count as corporate on Hachyderm, refuses handle parking, routes impersonation to reports, proposes a Mastodon collection of maintainers, and keeps maintainers on personal accounts.
expectations: States that Hachyderm treats CNCF or foundation-hosted projects as corporate accounts rather than free project accounts
Advises against reserving handles across servers, citing Hachyderm's parking ban or the futility across thousands of servers
States that collection members must have discovery turned on, or are notified and can remove themselves
Recommends reporting impersonators to the hosting server's moderators instead of reserving handles
Recommends a Mastodon collection (4.6+) as the shareable list of maintainers
States that a collection holds up to 25 accounts
States that Fosstodon is invite-only
Recommends each maintainer keep a personal account that discloses the project
Recommends rel=me verification between the project website and the project account
